title: Browser vs Search Engine
drDigitalIntro:
A browser and a search engine do different jobs — they are easy to mix up.
• The browser is the app you are using right now. It is the vehicle that carries you around the internet and shows you web pages.
• A search engine is a website you visit inside the browser. It helps you find other websites when you do not know their exact address.
• If you already know the address, skip the search engine — just type the address directly in the bar at the top and press Enter. You go straight there.
• If you do not know the address, go to a search engine like google.com, type what you are looking for, and pick from the list of results.
• Both methods use the same browser — the difference is knowing where you are going versus describing what you want to find.

playgroundTask.goal: Visit a site directly, then find one using a search engine

steps.say: When you know the address, type it directly. Type gardeningtips.example and press Enter — you go straight there.
When you do not know the address, use a search engine. Type google.com in the address bar and press Enter.
Now type what you are looking for in the search box: apple pie recipe — then press Enter.
Google gives you a list of results. Click Recipe Box to open that page.
steps.title: Recipe Box

drDigitalSuccess: You visited a site directly (by address) and found one using a search engine. Both use the browser — the difference is whether you know where you are going.
drDigitalHint: For the search step: click inside the search box on the google.com page, type apple pie recipe, and press Enter. Then click the Recipe Box result.
